<div class="sheet">
  <div class="ws-head">
    <div>
      <h1>Governance Readiness Self-Assessment (Six Capabilities)</h1>
      <p class="ws-sub">Score each capability. Name its owner and target date; list every capability at None as a floor violation.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-meta">
      <b>WS-05-governance-readiness-assessment</b><br>
      Pack E - Guardrails: authority, risk and proof<br>
      fill order <b>4</b> &middot; type <b>assessment</b><br>
      audience <b>mixed</b>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-source">
    Source: <b>Governance for AI-Assisted Delivery</b>, <i>Governance Readiness Checklist</i>
    &middot; <code>handbook/ch05-governance-for-ai-assisted-delivery.qmd</code> L31-71
    &middot; <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch05-governance-for-ai-assisted-delivery.html#sec-governance-readiness">#sec-governance-readiness</a>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    With the platform owner, security, compliance and the relevant tooling owners, score each capability from observable evidence. Carry the mandatory posture across from block B of the completed compliance scope matrix. Set a Basic or Enterprise target, a date, a named individual owner and the business risk of staying put. Record every None as a floor violation; name the dependency for any Enterprise target alongside its evidence. Complete block A before planning blocks B-D.
  </div>

  <div class="ws-block">
    <h2>Block A — the assessment
      <span class="ws-block-note">score what exists; evidence makes every score checkable</span></h2>

    <table class="ws">
      <colgroup>
        <col style="width:4%"><col style="width:16%"><col style="width:25%"><col style="width:25%"><col style="width:30%">
      </colgroup>
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th></th><th>Capability</th>
          <th>None — what it looks like</th>
          <th>Basic — what it looks like</th>
          <th>Enterprise — what it looks like</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">1</span></td>
          <td class="prior"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">Audit trails</span></div><span class="prior-src">ch05 L39</span></td>
          <td class="prior">No record of which code was agent-generated. Commits attributed to the prompting developer with no distinction.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L39</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Agent contributions tagged in commit metadata or PR labels. Prompt history retained for a defined period.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L39</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Full provenance chain: instruction given, context consumed, output produced, human review decision, and rationale — all queryable and linked to compliance artifacts. <i>Part III implements this as the agent-stack-trace and lockfile patterns.</i><span class="prior-src">ch05 L39</span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">2</span></td>
          <td class="prior"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">Agent access controls</span></div><span class="prior-src">ch05 L40</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Agents run with the developer's full credentials. No distinction between human and agent access scope.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L40</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Agents operate under scoped tokens with reduced permissions. File system and network access restricted to declared boundaries.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L40</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Least-privilege agent identities with per-task credential issuance, automatic expiration, and separate audit logging for agent actions. <i>Part III names the mechanism behind this row capability-based security — the runtime decides per-invocation which tools and contexts the agent can reach.</i><span class="prior-src">ch05 L40</span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">3</span></td>
          <td class="prior"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">Approval workflows</span></div><span class="prior-src">ch05 L41</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Standard code review applies identically to human and agent code. No additional scrutiny for agent output.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L41</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Agent-generated PRs are flagged for enhanced review. Critical paths (auth, payments, data access) require human sign-off regardless of author.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L41</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Risk-tiered review: agent output touching sensitive systems routed through security-aware reviewers with checklist-based verification. Approval latency tracked as a metric. <i>This is the strong-form supervision bar — the seam (the boundary where agent action meets the platform) is gated, not just observed.</i><span class="prior-src">ch05 L41</span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">4</span></td>
          <td class="prior"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">Data boundary enforcement</span></div><span class="prior-src">ch05 L42</span></td>
          <td class="prior">No controls on what data agents can access during code generation. Proprietary code, secrets, and customer data may enter agent context.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L42</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Agents restricted from accessing production data and secrets. Code sent to external models reviewed against data classification policy.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L42</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Data loss prevention integrated into agent workflows. Context filters prevent classified data from entering model prompts. Residency requirements enforced per jurisdiction. <i>Part III calls this discipline bounded-scope grounding — context is loaded with explicit provenance and an explicit boundary, not pulled in opportunistically.</i><span class="prior-src">ch05 L42</span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">5</span></td>
          <td class="prior"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">Cost controls</span></div><span class="prior-src">ch05 L43</span></td>
          <td class="prior">No visibility into agent-related compute or API spend. Costs absorbed into general cloud bills.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L43</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Per-team or per-project token budgets. Alerts on unusual consumption. Monthly cost reporting.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L43</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Real-time cost attribution per agent task. Automated circuit breakers on runaway sessions. Cost-per-feature tracking integrated into project planning.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L43</span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">6</span></td>
          <td class="prior"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">Compliance reporting</span></div><span class="prior-src">ch05 L44</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Cannot demonstrate to an auditor how agent-generated code is governed. Compliance posture unknown.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L44</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Periodic manual reports on agent usage, access scope, and review rates. Policies documented but enforcement is process-dependent.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L44</span></td>
          <td class="prior">Automated compliance dashboards. Agent governance artifacts generated alongside code. Audit-ready evidence exportable on demand. Policy enforcement is systemic, not procedural.<span class="prior-src">ch05 L44</span></td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>

    <p style="font-size:7.5pt;margin:1.5mm 0">
      <b>Scoring rule</b> (ch05 L54-69): Assess all six capabilities. If any is at
      <i>None</i>, start with audit trails and agent access controls; reassess quarterly.
      Otherwise, if all are at <i>Basic</i> or above, it is safe to expand agent adoption
      and invest toward Enterprise per regulatory scope. If not, start with audit trails
      and agent access controls. Most organizations at Phase 3 find at least four of six
      at None or Basic; that is expected, not a grade (ch05 L48).
    </p>
    <p style="font-size:7.5pt;margin:1.5mm 0">
      <b>A note on the Enterprise column.</b> The rightmost column describes a target state.
      Some of its requirements (full provenance chains, real-time cost attribution per agent
      task, automated compliance dashboards) exceed what current-generation tooling delivers
      out of the box. Treat the Enterprise column as directional, not immediate. When your
      compliance team asks "when do we get there," the honest answer is: some capabilities
      are available now with custom integration; others depend on tooling maturity that, as
      of mid-2025, remains ahead of generally available products. Plan accordingly, and do
      not let the aspiration prevent progress on Basic. (ch05 L50)
    </p>

  </div>
  <div class="ws-foot-quote">
    <i>The governance floor: no capability at "None" before expanding agent adoption. Start with audit trails and access controls — they unblock everything else.</i> (ch05 L71)
  </div>

      <p class="ws-sub">Assess the controls that must be in place before a third-party primitive is installed.</p></div>
    <div class="ws-meta">
      <b>WS-05-governance-readiness-assessment</b><br>

  <div class="ws-source">
